   185→        with:

   188→          tagName: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

   190→          releaseBody: 'Staging build for ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}. macOS (unsigned - right-click > Open to launch) and Windows (unsigned - click "More info" > "Run anyway").'

   195→    name: Build Desktop App (Windows)
   196→    needs: [create-desktop-release]
   197→    runs-on: windows-latest
   198→    environment: staging
   199→    permissions:
   200→      contents: write
   201→    steps:
   202→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
   203→        with:
   204→          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
   205→
   206→      - name: Install WinFsp
   207→        shell: powershell
   208→        run: |
   209→          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
   210→          # Use Join-Path to produce proper Windows backslash paths —
   211→          # msiexec.exe treats '/' as a flag prefix, so forward slashes in
   212→          # the file path cause "package could not be opened" errors.
   213→          $resourceDir = Join-Path "${{ github.workspace }}" "apps\desktop\src-tauri\resources"
   214→          $out = Join-Path $resourceDir "winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
   215→          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
   216→          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $resourceDir
   217→          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
   218→          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
   219→          if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch: expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash" }
   220→          $proc = Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","`"$out`"","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow -PassThru
   221→          if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0) { throw "msiexec failed with exit code $($proc.ExitCode)" }
   222→          # winfsp-sys build.rs reads HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp\InstallDir
   223→          # to find headers/libs. The MSI doesn't reliably write this key on CI runners.
   224→          $installDir = "C:\Program Files (x86)\WinFsp"
   225→          if (!(Test-Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp")) {
   226→            New-Item -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Force | Out-Null
   227→          }
   228→          New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Name "InstallDir" -Value $installDir -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
   229→          # Verify registry key was written correctly
   230→          $regVal = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Name "InstallDir" -ErrorAction Stop
   231→          if (-not $regVal.InstallDir -or $regVal.InstallDir -ne $installDir) {
   232→            throw "WinFsp InstallDir registry mismatch: expected '$installDir', got '$($regVal.InstallDir)'"

   520→          : "${DS_LOGS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID is required}"
   521→          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"
   522→
   523→          # The dashboard JSON uses __inputs for datasource templating.
   524→          # Replace variable references with actual datasource UIDs.
   525→          DASHBOARD=$(cat docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json \
   526→            | jq --arg metrics "$DS_METRICS_UID" --arg logs "$DS_LOGS_UID" \
   527→                 'del(.__inputs)
   528→                  | .id = null
   529→                  | walk(if type == "object" and .uid? and (.uid | test("\\$\\{DS_")) then
   530→                      .uid = (if .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_METRICS}" then $metrics
   531→                              elif .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_LOGS}" then $logs
   532→                              else .uid end)
   533→                    else . end)')
   534→
   535→          # Fail if any datasource placeholder survived the rewrite
   536→          if jq -e '.. | objects | .uid? | select(type == "string" and test("^\\$\\{DS_"))' \
   537→            >/dev/null <<<"$DASHBOARD"; then
   538→            echo "::error::Unresolved datasource placeholder(s) remain in dashboard JSON"
   539→            exit 1
   540→          fi
   541→
   542→          # Wrap in import payload
   543→          PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --argjson dashboard "$DASHBOARD" '{
   544→            dashboard: $dashboard,
   545→            overwrite: true,
   546→            message: "Provisioned by deploy-staging workflow"
   547→          }')
   548→

   553→            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
   554→            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

   559→            cat /tmp/grafana-response.json
   560→            exit 1
   561→          fi

   563→          echo "Dashboard provisioned successfully (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)"
   564→          jq -r '.url // "unknown"' /tmp/grafana-response.json

1→# Environment Architecture
     2→
     3→**Created:** 2026-01-25
     4→
     5→## Overview
     6→
     7→CipherBox requires isolated environments to prevent cross-environment interference, particularly with IPNS sequence numbers. This document defines the environment architecture and solves the Web3Auth key isolation problem.
     8→
     9→## The Problem
    10→
    11→**Current State:** All environments share the same Web3Auth project (SAPPHIRE_DEVNET) and client ID. This means:
    12→
    13→- Same user identity → same derived secp256k1 keypair → same Ed25519 IPNS keypair
    14→- IPNS records use monotonically increasing sequence numbers
    15→- If CI publishes seq=100, local dev (fresh DB) tries seq=1 → rejected by network/delegated routing
    16→- Test repeatability is impossible without manual intervention
    17→
    18→## Environment Matrix
    19→
    20→| Environment    | IPFS Mode      | Web3Auth Network | IPNS Routing           | Database            | TEE Republishing     | Isolation Level            |
    21→| -------------- | -------------- | ---------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------- |
    22→| **Local Dev**  | Kubo (offline) | Sapphire Devnet  | Mock service           | Local Postgres      | **Disabled**         | Full                       |
    23→| **CI E2E**     | Kubo (offline) | Sapphire Devnet  | Mock service (per-run) | Ephemeral Postgres  | **Disabled**         | Full per-run               |
    24→| **Staging**    | Kubo (online)  | Sapphire Devnet  | Self-hosted Someguy    | Managed Postgres    | **Active** (testnet) | Shared with Local/CI users |
    25→| **Production** | Kubo (managed) | Sapphire Mainnet | delegated-ipfs.dev     | Production Postgres | **Active** (mainnet) | Full                       |
    26→
    27→## Solution: Environment-Aware Key Derivation
    28→
    29→### Recommended Approach: Environment-Specific IPNS Key Derivation
    30→
    31→The IPNS keypair is derived from the user's vault key. By adding an environment-specific context (via the HKDF `info` parameter) to this derivation, we get different IPNS keys per environment while keeping the same Web3Auth identity.
    32→
    33→**Key Insight:** The problematic shared state is the **IPNS keypair**, not the user's encryption keypair. We can:
    34→
    35→1. Keep the same secp256k1 keypair from Web3Auth (same encryption keys)
    36→2. Add environment context only to Ed25519 IPNS key derivation (different IPNS identities)
    37→
    38→This means:
    39→
    40→- Same user can encrypt/decrypt files across environments (if CIDs are known)
    41→  - **Security Note:** CID leakage can expose test or production data across environments. Use separate test accounts/credentials for CI vs production, and sanitize or isolate test data to avoid accidental cross-environment access.
    42→- Different IPNS namespaces per environment → no sequence conflicts
    43→- Test accounts work in all environments without conflicts
    44→
    45→### Implementation
    46→
    47→```typescript
    48→// packages/crypto/src/ipns.ts
    49→
    50→// Fixed HKDF salt for domain separation (extract phase)
    51→const HKDF_SALT = 'CipherBox-IPNS-v1';
    52→
    53→// Environment context prefixes for HKDF info (expand phase)
    54→const ENVIRONMENT_CONTEXT = {
    55→  local: 'env:local',
    56→  ci: 'env:ci',
    57→  staging: 'env:staging',
    58→  production: 'env:production',
    59→} as const;
    60→
    61→type Environment = keyof typeof ENVIRONMENT_CONTEXT;
    62→
    63→export function deriveIpnsKeypair(
    64→  userSecp256k1PrivateKey: Uint8Array,
    65→  folderId: string,
    66→  environment: Environment
    67→): { publicKey: Uint8Array; privateKey: Uint8Array } {
    68→  // HKDF-SHA256: Fixed salt for domain separation, environment/folder in info for context binding
    69→  // This follows RFC 5869 best practices and matches existing deriveKey patterns in the codebase
    70→  const info = `${ENVIRONMENT_CONTEXT[environment]}:folder:${folderId}`;
    71→  // ... derivation logic using HKDF(IKM=userSecp256k1PrivateKey, salt=HKDF_SALT, info=info)
    72→}
    73→```
    74→
    75→**Configuration:**
    76→
    77→```bash
    78→# .env
    79→CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=local  # local | ci | staging | production
    80→```
    81→
    82→### Alternative: Separate Web3Auth Projects
    83→
    84→If you prefer complete user isolation (different user databases per environment):
    85→
    86→| Environment | Web3Auth Project  | Network          | Client ID  |
    87→| ----------- | ----------------- | ---------------- | ---------- |
    88→| Local/CI    | cipherbox-dev     | Sapphire Devnet  | `BK...dev` |
    89→| Staging     | cipherbox-staging | Sapphire Devnet  | `BK...stg` |
    90→| Production  | cipherbox-prod    | Sapphire Mainnet | `BK...prd` |
    91→
    92→**Pros:**
    93→
    94→- Complete isolation including encryption keys
    95→- No code changes needed (just config)
    96→- Clear separation of concerns
    97→
    98→**Cons:**
    99→
   100→- Need separate test accounts per environment
   101→- Can't share encrypted data between environments
   102→- More Web3Auth dashboard management
   103→
   104→## Detailed Environment Specifications
   105→
   106→### 1. Local Development Environment
   107→
   108→**Purpose:** Isolated development with persistent state, no network dependencies
   109→
   110→**Infrastructure:**
   111→
   112→```yaml
   113→# docker/docker-compose.local.yml
   114→services:
   115→  postgres:
   116→    image: postgres:16-alpine
   117→    environment:
   118→      POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_local
   119→    ports:
   120→      - '5432:5432'
   121→    volumes:
   122→      - postgres_local_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
   123→
   124→  ipfs:
   125→    image: ipfs/kubo:v0.34.0
   126→    command: daemon --offline # KEY: Offline mode
   127→    ports:
   128→      - '127.0.0.1:5001:5001' # API
   129→      - '127.0.0.1:8080:8080' # Gateway
   130→    volumes:
   131→      - ipfs_local_data:/data/ipfs
   132→
   133→  mock-ipns-routing:
   134→    build: ../tools/mock-ipns-routing
   135→    ports:
   136→      - '127.0.0.1:3001:3001'
   137→    volumes:
   138→      - mock_ipns_data:/data # Persistent mock IPNS records
   139→
   140→volumes:
   141→  postgres_local_data:
   142→  ipfs_local_data:
   143→  mock_ipns_data:
   144→```
   145→
   146→**Configuration:**
   147→
   148→```bash
   149→# apps/web/.env.local
   150→VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID=BK...dev  # Devnet client ID
   151→VITE_API_URL=http://localhost:3000
   152→VITE_ENVIRONMENT=local
   153→
   154→# apps/api/.env.local
   155→NODE_ENV=development
   156→CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=local
   157→DB_HOST=localhost
   158→DB_PORT=5432
   159→DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_local
   160→IPFS_PROVIDER=local
   161→IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL=http://localhost:5001
   162→IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL=http://localhost:8080
   163→DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://localhost:3001
   164→REDACTED
   165→```
   166→
   167→**Characteristics:**
   168→
   169→- Kubo runs with `--offline` flag (no DHT, no peer connections)
   170→- Mock IPNS routing with persistent storage (survives restarts)
   171→- Local Postgres with persistent volume
   172→- Environment context: `local`
   173→
   174→### 2. CI E2E Testing Environment
   175→
   176→**Purpose:** Isolated, reproducible test runs with fresh state each time
   177→
   178→**GitHub Actions Configuration:**
   179→
   180→```yaml
   181→# .github/workflows/e2e.yml
   182→services:
   183→  postgres:
   184→    image: postgres:16-alpine
   185→    env:
   186→      POSTGRES_DB: cipherbox_ci
   187→    options: >-
   188→      --health-cmd pg_isready
   189→      --health-interval 5s
   190→      --health-timeout 5s
   191→      --health-retries 5
   192→
   193→  ipfs:
   194→    image: ipfs/kubo:v0.34.0
   195→    # No --offline needed in CI (isolated network anyway)
   196→    # No volume mounts (ephemeral state)
   197→    options: >-
   198→      --health-cmd "ipfs id"
   199→      --health-interval 10s
   200→      --health-timeout 5s
   201→      --health-retries 10
   202→
   203→env:

   420→## TEE Infrastructure by Environment
   421→
   422→The TEE (Trusted Execution Environment) layer handles IPNS republishing to prevent record expiry (24-hour TTL). This section defines TEE requirements per environment.
   423→
   424→### TEE Environment Matrix
   425→
   426→| Environment    | TEE Infrastructure     | IPNS Republishing | Monitoring        | Cleanup                    |
   427→| -------------- | ---------------------- | ----------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------- |
   428→| **Local Dev**  | None                   | Not needed        | None              | User resets to clean slate |
   429→| **CI E2E**     | None                   | Not needed        | None              | Ephemeral per-run          |
   430→| **Staging**    | Active (Phala testnet) | Every 3 hours     | Integration tests | Periodic DHT cleanup       |
   431→| **Production** | Active (Phala mainnet) | Every 3 hours     | Full alerting     | Automated stale detection  |

   663→
   664→### TEE Key Encryption Architecture
   665→
   666→This section documents the security architecture for encrypting IPNS private keys before transmission to the TEE for republishing.
   667→
   668→#### Threat Model
   669→
   670→**Assets:**
   671→
   672→- IPNS private keys (Ed25519) - control over user's folder metadata
   673→- User's ability to update IPNS records
   674→
   675→**Threats:**
   676→
   677→1. **Network interception:** Attacker intercepts IPNS private key in transit to TEE
   678→2. **TEE key compromise:** Attacker obtains TEE private key, can decrypt all `encryptedIpnsPrivateKey` values
   679→3. **Stale epoch attack:** Attacker replays old encrypted keys after epoch rotation
   680→
   681→**Security Goals:**
   682→
   683→- IPNS private keys are never transmitted in plaintext
   684→- Only the current TEE can decrypt keys (forward secrecy via epoch rotation)
   685→- Key compromise has bounded impact (4-week epoch window)
   686→
   687→#### Encryption Flow
   688→
   689→```text
   690→User Client                      CipherBox API                    TEE (Phala Cloud)
   691→    |                                 |                                 |
   692→    |  1. Fetch TEE public key        |                                 |
   693→    |-------------------------------->|                                 |
   694→    |                                 |  2. Get current epoch key       |
   695→    |                                 |-------------------------------->|
   696→    |                                 |<--------------------------------|
   697→    |<--------------------------------|  {publicKey, epoch}             |
   698→    |                                 |                                 |
   699→    |  3. ECIES encrypt IPNS key      |                                 |
   700→    |  with TEE public key            |                                 |
   701→    |                                 |                                 |
   702→    |  4. POST /folders/:id/publish   |                                 |
   703→    |  {encryptedIpnsPrivateKey,      |                                 |
   704→    |   keyEpoch, ipnsValue, ...}     |                                 |
   705→    |-------------------------------->|                                 |
   706→    |                                 |  5. Store for republishing      |
   707→    |                                 |  (cron every 3 hours)           |
   708→    |                                 |                                 |
   709→    |                                 |  6. Send encrypted key to TEE   |
   710→    |                                 |-------------------------------->|
   711→    |                                 |                                 |  7. Decrypt in hardware
   712→    |                                 |                                 |  8. Sign IPNS record
   713→    |                                 |                                 |  9. Discard key (never stored)
   714→    |                                 |<--------------------------------|
   715→    |                                 |  {signedIpnsRecord}             |
   716→```
   717→
   718→#### Encryption Primitive: ECIES over secp256k1
   719→
   720→Per project security standards, IPNS private keys MUST be encrypted using ECIES (Elliptic Curve Integrated Encryption Scheme) with secp256k1:
   721→
   722→```typescript
   723→// packages/crypto/src/tee/encrypt.ts
   724→import { eciesEncrypt } from '../ecies';
   725→
   726→export async function encryptIpnsKeyForTee(
   727→  ipnsPrivateKey: Uint8Array, // 32-byte Ed25519 private key
   728→  teePublicKey: Uint8Array, // secp256k1 public key (33 or 65 bytes)
   729→  keyEpoch: number // Current TEE key epoch
   730→): Promise<EncryptedIpnsKey> {
   731→  // ECIES encryption: ephemeral ECDH + AES-256-GCM
   732→  const ciphertext = await eciesEncrypt(ipnsPrivateKey, teePublicKey);
   733→
   734→  return {
   735→    ciphertext,
   736→    keyEpoch,
   737→    algorithm: 'ECIES-secp256k1-AES256GCM',
   738→  };
   739→}
   740→```
   741→
   742→#### TEE Public Key Distribution
   743→
   744→The TEE public key is obtained via the CipherBox API, which caches and validates it from Phala Cloud:
   745→
   746→```typescript
   747→// apps/api/src/tee/tee.service.ts
   748→export class TeeService {
   749→  private cachedPublicKey: { key: Uint8Array; epoch: number; expiresAt: Date } | null = null;
   750→
   751→  async getCurrentPublicKey(): Promise<{ publicKey: Uint8Array; epoch: number }> {
   752→    // 1. Check cache (valid for 1 hour)
   753→    if (this.cachedPublicKey && this.cachedPublicKey.expiresAt > new Date()) {
   754→      return { publicKey: this.cachedPublicKey.key, epoch: this.cachedPublicKey.epoch };
   755→    }
   756→
   757→    // 2. Fetch from Phala Cloud with attestation verification
   758→    const response = await this.phalaClient.getPublicKey();
   759→
   760→    // 3. Verify attestation quote (proves key is from genuine TEE)
   761→    await this.verifyAttestation(response.attestation);
   762→
   763→    // 4. Cache with expiry
   764→    this.cachedPublicKey = {
   765→      key: response.publicKey,
   766→      epoch: response.epoch,
   767→      expiresAt: new Date(Date.now() + 60 * 60 * 1000), // 1 hour
   768→    };
   769→
   770→    return { publicKey: response.publicKey, epoch: response.epoch };
   771→  }
   772→}
   773→```
   774→
   775→#### Key Epoch Rotation Scheme
   776→
   777→TEE keys rotate every 4 weeks (`TEE_KEY_EPOCH_ROTATION_WEEKS=4`) with a 1-week grace period:
   778→
   779→| Epoch State      | Window    | API Behavior                                     |
   780→| ---------------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
   781→| Current          | Weeks 0-4 | Normal processing                                |
   782→| Previous (grace) | Weeks 4-5 | Accept, re-encrypt with new epoch, update record |
   783→| Expired          | >5 weeks  | Reject with `EPOCH_EXPIRED` error                |
   784→
   785→**Epoch Handling Logic:**
   786→
   787→```typescript
   788→// apps/api/src/tee/epoch.service.ts
   789→export class EpochService {
   790→  private readonly GRACE_PERIOD_WEEKS = 1;
   791→
   792→  async validateEpoch(submittedEpoch: number): Promise<EpochValidation> {
   793→    const currentEpoch = await this.getCurrentEpoch();
   794→
   795→    if (submittedEpoch === currentEpoch) {
   796→      return { valid: true, action: 'PROCESS_NORMALLY' };
   797→    }
   798→
   799→    if (submittedEpoch === currentEpoch - 1) {
   800→      const gracePeriodEnd = this.getEpochEndDate(currentEpoch - 1).add(
   801→        this.GRACE_PERIOD_WEEKS,
   802→        'weeks'
   803→      );
   804→
   805→      if (new Date() < gracePeriodEnd) {
   806→        return { valid: true, action: 'RE_ENCRYPT_AND_UPDATE' };
   807→      }
   808→    }
   809→
   810→    return {
   811→      valid: false,
   812→      action: 'REJECT',
   813→      error: {
   814→        code: 'EPOCH_EXPIRED',
   815→        message: 'TEE key epoch expired. Fetch new TEE public key and re-encrypt.',
   816→        currentEpoch,
   817→      },
   818→    };
   819→  }
   820→}
   821→```
   822→
   823→**Grace Period Expiration:**
   824→Records encrypted with an expired epoch that were not re-encrypted during the grace period become invalid. The TEE cannot decrypt them, and the republishing job will:
   825→
   826→1. Mark the record as `republish_failed` with reason `EPOCH_EXPIRED`
   827→2. Send alert to monitoring (PagerDuty/Opsgenie)
   828→3. User must re-publish from client to restore republishing
   829→
   830→#### Forward Secrecy Considerations
   831→
   832→- **Epoch rotation provides bounded compromise:** If a TEE private key is compromised, only records encrypted with that epoch's key are exposed
   833→- **No retroactive decryption:** Old epoch keys are destroyed; past ciphertexts cannot be decrypted
   834→- **Grace period tradeoff:** 1-week grace period balances usability (client update propagation) vs security (exposure window)

     9→Phase 19 replaces the external `delegated-ipfs.dev` delegated routing service with a self-hosted Someguy instance running as a Docker Compose sidecar.    162→**What:** Change `DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL` from the external service to the internal Docker service name.
   163→
   164→**When to use:** When swapping an external dependency with an internal one that implements the same API contract.
   165→
   166→**Example in deploy-staging.yml:**
   167→```yaml
   168→# Before:
   169→DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=https://delegated-ipfs.dev
   170→# After:
   171→DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190
   172→```
   173→
   174→**Key details:**
   175→- The `DelegatedRoutingClient` reads this URL at constructor time via `ConfigService`
   176→- The URL path `/routing/v1/ipns/{name}` is appended by the client, not included in the env var
   177→- E2E tests continue using `http://localhost:3001` (the mock service) -- no E2E change needed
   178→- Local development can continue using `https://delegated-ipfs.dev` or the mock service
   179→
   180→### Pattern 3: Prometheus Histogram for Operation Latency
   181→
   182→**What:** Add dedicated histograms to track Someguy resolution/publish latency and outcome.
   183→
   184→**When to use:** When you need p50/p95/p99 latency data for a specific operation, not just success/failure counts.
   185→
   186→**Example:**
   187→```typescript
   188→// Source: existing MetricsService patterns in metrics.service.ts
   189→// New histograms to add alongside existing counters
   190→readonly ipnsPublishDuration: client.Histogram;
   191→readonly ipnsResolveDuration: client.Histogram;
   192→
   193→// In constructor:
   194→this.ipnsPublishDuration = new client.Histogram({
   195→  name: 'cipherbox_ipns_publish_duration_seconds',
   196→  help: 'IPNS publish duration in seconds',
   197→  labelNames: ['outcome'],  // 'success', 'error', 'timeout'
   198→  buckets: [0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30, 60],
   199→  registers: [this.registry],
   200→});
   201→
   202→this.ipnsResolveDuration = new client.Histogram({
   203→  name: 'cipherbox_ipns_resolve_duration_seconds',
   204→  help: 'IPNS resolve duration in seconds',
   205→  labelNames: ['source'],  // 'network', 'db_cache', 'network_stale'
   206→  buckets: [0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10, 30],
   207→  registers: [this.registry],
   208→});
   209→```
   210→
   211→**Label design:**
   212→- `ipnsPublishDuration` labels: `outcome` = `success` | `error` | `timeout`
   213→- `ipnsResolveDuration` labels: `source` = `network` (Someguy returned result) | `db_cache` (fell back to DB) | `network_stale` (network returned but DB was newer)
   214→- Keep cardinality low -- no per-ipnsName labels

   216→### Anti-Patterns to Avoid
   217→
   218→- **Setting `SOMEGUY_DHT=accelerated` in staging:** The accelerated DHT client crawls the entire Amino DHT (30k+ peers, 12+ hours warm-up, 2GB+ memory). Use `standard` for staging, reserve `accelerated` for production if needed.
   219→- **Exposing Someguy ports to the host:** Someguy only needs to be reachable from the `api` container. Exposing `8190` to the host is unnecessary and increases attack surface.
   220→- **Adding `depends_on: someguy` to the `api` service:** While the API depends on Someguy, it already handles routing failures gracefully (DB fallback). A hard dependency would prevent the API from starting if Someguy is slow to initialize. Use a soft dependency or no dependency.
   221→- **Changing resolution logic simultaneously with the URL swap:** Per CONTEXT.md, keep identical timeout/retry config for apples-to-apples comparison with Phase 18 baselines.

   223→## Don't Hand-Roll
   224→
   225→| Problem                          | Don't Build                              | Use Instead                        | Why                                                                                               |
   226→| -------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
   227→| Delegated routing server         | Custom HTTP proxy to Kubo's DHT          | Someguy v0.11.1                    | Someguy IS the reference implementation. Maintained by IPFS Foundation. Same spec as delegated-ipfs.dev. |
   228→| DHT client                       | Custom libp2p DHT node in Node.js        | Someguy's embedded Go DHT client   | Go implementation is battle-tested (same code as Kubo). JS DHT client has known reliability issues. |
   229→| Health check endpoint for Someguy| Custom sidecar that polls Someguy        | Docker healthcheck on `/version`   | Simpler, built-in to Docker Compose, no extra container needed.                                    |
   230→| Metrics for routing latency      | Custom timing wrapper around fetch       | prom-client Histogram + `observe()`| Existing pattern in MetricsService. Consistent with httpRequestDuration histogram.                 |
   231→
   232→**Key insight:** The entire Phase 19 infrastructure change is adding one Docker container and changing one environment variable. The `DelegatedRoutingClient` abstraction already exists -- don't bypass it.
   233→
   234→## Common Pitfalls
   235→
   236→### Pitfall 1: Someguy Default Listen Address is 127.0.0.1
   237→
   238→**What goes wrong:** Someguy defaults to `SOMEGUY_LISTEN_ADDRESS=127.0.0.1:8190`. Inside a Docker container, `127.0.0.1` means "only this container." The `api` container cannot reach it.
   239→**Why it happens:** Someguy follows Go convention of binding to localhost by default for security.
   240→**How to avoid:** Set `SOMEGUY_LISTEN_ADDRESS=0.0.0.0:8190` in the Docker Compose environment.
   241→**Warning signs:** `ECONNREFUSED` when `api` tries to connect to `http://someguy:8190`.
   242→
   243→### Pitfall 2: Accelerated DHT Mode Resource Consumption
   244→
   245→**What goes wrong:** Someguy with `SOMEGUY_DHT=accelerated` (the default) performs a full DHT crawl on startup, consuming 2GB+ memory and significant CPU/bandwidth for 12+ hours.
   246→**Why it happens:** Accelerated mode builds a complete routing table for sub-second lookups -- great for public infrastructure, overkill for a single-app sidecar.
   247→**How to avoid:** Set `SOMEGUY_DHT=standard` for staging. Consider `accelerated` only for production if standard mode latency is unacceptable.
   248→**Warning signs:** Someguy container OOM-killed shortly after startup. High bandwidth usage from the VPS.
   249→
   250→### Pitfall 3: Someguy Has No /health Endpoint
   251→
   252→**What goes wrong:** Docker Compose health checks using `wget -qO- http://localhost:8190/health` fail with 404, causing container restarts.
   253→**Why it happens:** Someguy only exposes `/routing/v1/*`, `/debug/metrics/prometheus`, and `/version`. No health endpoint.
   254→**How to avoid:** Use `/version` for health checks: `wget -qO- http://localhost:8190/version || exit 1`.
   255→**Warning signs:** Container stuck in "starting" state, repeated restarts in Docker logs.
   256→
   257→### Pitfall 4: Someguy Needs Outbound Internet Access for DHT
   258→
   259→**What goes wrong:** Someguy cannot resolve any IPNS names because it cannot connect to DHT bootstrap peers.
   260→**Why it happens:** Docker network configuration or firewall blocks outbound connections from the `someguy` container.
   261→**How to avoid:** Ensure the Docker network allows outbound connections (default bridge network does). Someguy uses libp2p ports 4001/udp + TCP for DHT. It does NOT need inbound ports -- DHT client mode works with outbound-only connections.
   262→**Warning signs:** Someguy logs show "failed to bootstrap" or "no peers found". IPNS resolution returns 404 for known names.
   263→
   264→### Pitfall 5: Deploy-Staging Workflow Hardcodes DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL
   265→
   266→**What goes wrong:** After updating `docker-compose.staging.yml`, the deploy workflow still writes `DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=https://delegated-ipfs.dev` to `.env.staging`, overriding the intended Someguy URL.
   267→**Why it happens:** The URL is hardcoded at line 377 of `deploy-staging.yml` in the `Generate .env.staging` step.
   268→**How to avoid:** Change the hardcoded value to `http://someguy:8190` in the deploy workflow.
   269→**Warning signs:** After deployment, API logs still show connections to `delegated-ipfs.dev` instead of `someguy:8190`.
   270→
   271→### Pitfall 6: Timing Metrics Not Instrumenting the Right Layer
   272→
   273→**What goes wrong:** Latency histograms placed at the controller level include HTTP overhead and serialization, making Someguy resolution look slower than it is. Or, placed only inside `DelegatedRoutingClient`, they miss DB fallback timing.
   274→**Why it happens:** Unclear about which layer represents the "IPNS resolution duration" from the user's perspective.
   275→**How to avoid:** Instrument at the `IpnsService.resolveRecord()` level for end-to-end resolution timing (includes network attempt + possible DB fallback). Add a second histogram at `DelegatedRoutingClient.resolve()` for pure Someguy latency. Both histograms together tell the full story.
   276→**Warning signs:** Metrics show Someguy latency of 50ms but API p95 for `/ipns/resolve` is 2s -- the gap is the DB query + serialization overhead.

   401→## Open Questions
   402→
   403→1. **Someguy libp2p port requirements in Docker**
   404→   - What we know: Someguy runs its own libp2p node. DHT client mode works with outbound-only connections.
   405→   - What's unclear: Whether Docker's default bridge network allows sufficient outbound UDP connections for DHT bootstrap. No documentation specifically addresses Docker deployment.
   406→   - Recommendation: Deploy with default Docker networking. If DHT fails to bootstrap, try adding `network_mode: host` or exposing UDP port 4001 (same as Kubo's swarm port -- use a different port to avoid conflict).
   407→
   408→2. **Someguy warm-up time for standard DHT mode**
   409→   - What we know: Accelerated mode takes 12+ hours to warm up. Standard mode is faster but no published benchmarks.
   410→   - What's unclear: How long until Someguy in standard mode can resolve an existing IPNS name after cold start.
   411→   - Recommendation: Plan for a 1-2 minute warm-up period after deployment. The start_period in health check (30s) should cover initial bootstrap. If early resolution fails, DB fallback handles it.
   412→
   413→3. **Whether to scrape Someguy's Prometheus metrics**
   414→   - What we know: Someguy exposes `/debug/metrics/prometheus` with its own metrics (routing client latency, response sizes as of v0.9.1).
   415→   - What's unclear: Whether these metrics are useful alongside the application-level histograms.
   416→   - Recommendation: Optionally add a second `prometheus.scrape` target in `alloy-config.river` for Someguy. Low effort, potentially useful for debugging DHT issues. Not blocking.

content.content:
name: cipherbox-staging

x-logging: &default-logging
  driver: json-file
  options:
    max-size: '10m'
    max-file: '3'

services:
  api:
    image: ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER:-OWNER}/cipherbox-api:${TAG:-latest}
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file: .env.staging
    ports:
      - '127.0.0.1:3000:3000'
    logging: *default-logging
    depends_on:
      postgres:
        condition: service_healthy
      redis:
        condition: service_healthy

  postgres:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: ${DB_USERNAME:-cipherbox}
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD}
      POSTGRES_DB: ${DB_DATABASE:-cipherbox_staging}
    ports:
      - '127.0.0.1:5432:5432'
    volumes:
      - postgres_staging:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    logging: *default-logging
    healthcheck:
      test:

1→name: Deploy Staging
     2→
     3→on:
     4→  push:
     5→    tags:
     6→      - 'v*-staging*'
     7→  workflow_call:
     8→    inputs:
     9→      staging_tag:
    10→        required: true
    11→        type: string
    12→
    13→env:
    14→  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
    15→  # Resolve tag: workflow_call passes it as input, push trigger uses ref_name
    16→  DEPLOY_TAG: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
    17→
    18→jobs:
    19→  build-api:
    20→    name: Build & Push API Image
    21→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    22→    permissions:
    23→      contents: read
    24→      packages: write
    25→    steps:
    26→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    27→        with:
    28→          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
    29→
    30→      - name: Set lowercase image name
    31→        run: echo "API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-api" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    32→
    33→      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
    34→        with:
    35→          registry: ghcr.io
    36→          username: ${{ github.actor }}
    37→          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    38→
    39→      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
    40→        with:
    41→          context: .
    42→          file: apps/api/Dockerfile
    43→          push: true
    44→          tags: |
    45→            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}
    46→            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:latest
    47→
    48→  build-tee:
    49→    name: Build & Push TEE Worker Image
    50→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    51→    permissions:
    52→      contents: read
    53→      packages: write
    54→    steps:
    55→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    56→        with:
    57→          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
    58→
    59→      - name: Set lowercase image name
    60→        run: echo "TEE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-tee-worker" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
    61→
    62→      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
    63→        with:
    64→          registry: ghcr.io
    65→          username: ${{ github.actor }}
    66→          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
    67→
    68→      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
    69→        with:
    70→          context: ./tee-worker
    71→          file: tee-worker/Dockerfile
    72→          push: true
    73→          tags: |
    74→            ${{ env.TEE_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}
    75→            ${{ env.TEE_IMAGE }}:latest
    76→
    77→  build-web:
    78→    name: Build Web App
    79→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    80→    environment: staging
    81→    steps:
    82→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    83→        with:
    84→          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
    85→
    86→      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
    87→        with:
    88→          version: 10
    89→
    90→      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
    91→        with:
    92→          node-version: '22'
    93→          cache: 'pnpm'
    94→
    95→      - name: Install dependencies
    96→        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
    97→
    98→      - name: Build shared packages
    99→        run: |
   100→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
   101→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
   102→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
   103→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
   104→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build
   105→
   106→      - name: Build web app with staging env vars
   107→        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build
   108→        env:
   109→          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
   110→          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
   111→          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
   112→          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
   113→
   114→      - name: Upload web dist as artifact
   115→        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
   116→        with:
   117→          name: web-dist
   118→          path: apps/web/dist/
   119→          retention-days: 1
   120→
   121→  create-desktop-release:
   122→    name: Create Desktop Release
   123→    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
   124→    permissions:
   125→      contents: write
   126→    steps:
   127→      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
   128→        env:
   129→          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   130→        run: |
   131→          TAG="${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}"
   132→          BODY="Staging build for ${TAG}. macOS (unsigned - right-click > Open to launch), Windows (unsigned - click \"More info\" > \"Run anyway\"), and Linux (AppImage/deb)."
   133→          # Create the release if it doesn't exist yet; ignore error if it does
   134→          gh release create "$TAG" \
   135→            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
   136→            --title "CipherBox Desktop ${TAG}" \
   137→            --notes "$BODY" \
   138→            --prerelease 2>/dev/null || true
   139→
   140→  build-desktop:
   141→    name: Build Desktop App (macOS)
   142→    needs: [create-desktop-release]
   143→    runs-on: macos-latest
   144→    environment: staging
   145→    permissions:
   146→      contents: write
   147→    steps:
   148→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
   149→        with:
   150→          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
   151→
   152→      - name: Install FUSE-T
   153→        run: |
   154→          brew install --cask fuse-t
   155→          sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig
   156→          sudo ln -sf "/Library/Application Support/fuse-t/pkgconfig/fuse-t.pc" /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc
   157→
   158→      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
   159→        with:
   160→          version: 10
   161→
   162→      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
   163→        with:
   164→          node-version: '22'
   165→          cache: 'pnpm'
   166→
   167→      - name: Install dependencies
   168→        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
   169→
   170→      - name: Build shared packages
   171→        run: |
   172→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
   173→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
   174→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
   175→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
   176→          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build
   177→
   178→      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
   179→        env:
   180→          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
   181→          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
   182→          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
   183→          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
   184→          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
   185→        with:
   186→          projectPath: apps/desktop
   187→          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
   188→          tagName: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
   189→          releaseName: 'CipherBox Desktop ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}'
   190→          releaseBody: 'Staging build for ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}. macOS (unsigned - right-click > Open to launch) and Windows (unsigned - click "More info" > "Run anyway").'
   191→          releaseDraft: false
   192→          prerelease: true
   193→
   194→  build-desktop-windows:
   195→    name: Build Desktop App (Windows)
   196→    needs: [create-desktop-release]
   197→    runs-on: windows-latest
   198→    environment: staging
   199→    permissions:
   200→      contents: write
   201→    steps:
   202→      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
   203→        with:
   204→          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
   205→
   206→      - name: Install WinFsp
   207→        shell: powershell
   208→        run: |
   209→          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
   210→          # Use Join-Path to produce proper Windows backslash paths —
   211→          # msiexec.exe treats '/' as a flag prefix, so forward slashes in
   212→          # the file path cause "package could not be opened" errors.
   213→          $resourceDir = Join-Path "${{ github.workspace }}" "apps\desktop\src-tauri\resources"
   214→          $out = Join-Path $resourceDir "winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
   215→          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
   216→          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $resourceDir
   217→          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
   218→          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash

name: Deploy Staging

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*-staging*'
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      staging_tag:
        required: true
        type: string

env:
  REGISTRY: ghcr.io
  # Resolve tag: workflow_call passes it as input, push trigger uses ref_name
  DEPLOY_TAG: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

jobs:
  build-api:
    name: Build & Push API Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Set lowercase image name
        run: echo "API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-api" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          file: apps/api/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}
            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:latest

  build-tee:
    name: Build & Push TEE Worker Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Set lowercase image name
        run: echo "TEE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-tee-worker" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: ./tee-worker
          file: tee-worker/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ env.TEE_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}
            ${{ env.TEE_IMAGE }}:latest

  build-web:
    name: Build Web App
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build shared packages
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build

      - name: Build web app with staging env vars
        run: pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web build
        env:
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}

      - name: Upload web dist as artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: web-dist
          path: apps/web/dist/
          retention-days: 1

  create-desktop-release:
    name: Create Desktop Release
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - name: Create or update GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          TAG="${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}"
          BODY="Staging build for ${TAG}. macOS (unsigned - right-click > Open to launch), Windows (unsigned - click \"More info\" > \"Run anyway\"), and Linux (AppImage/deb)."
          # Create the release if it doesn't exist yet; ignore error if it does
          gh release create "$TAG" \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}" \
            --title "CipherBox Desktop ${TAG}" \
            --notes "$BODY" \
            --prerelease 2>/dev/null || true

  build-desktop:
    name: Build Desktop App (macOS)
    needs: [create-desktop-release]
    runs-on: macos-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Install FUSE-T
        run: |
          brew install --cask fuse-t
          sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig
          sudo ln -sf "/Library/Application Support/fuse-t/pkgconfig/fuse-t.pc" /usr/local/lib/pkgconfig/fuse.pc

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build shared packages
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}
          VITE_API_URL: ${{ vars.STAGING_API_URL }}
          VITE_ENVIRONMENT: staging
          VITE_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
        with:
          projectPath: apps/desktop
          tauriScript: pnpm tauri
          tagName: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}
          releaseName: 'CipherBox Desktop ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}'
          releaseBody: 'Staging build for ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}. macOS (unsigned - right-click > Open to launch) and Windows (unsigned - click "More info" > "Run anyway").'
          releaseDraft: false
          prerelease: true

  build-desktop-windows:
    name: Build Desktop App (Windows)
    needs: [create-desktop-release]
    runs-on: windows-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Install WinFsp
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          # Use Join-Path to produce proper Windows backslash paths —
          # msiexec.exe treats '/' as a flag prefix, so forward slashes in
          # the file path cause "package could not be opened" errors.
          $resourceDir = Join-Path "${{ github.workspace }}" "apps\desktop\src-tauri\resources"
          $out = Join-Path $resourceDir "winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $resourceDir
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
          if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch: expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash" }
          $proc = Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","`"$out`"","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow -PassThru
          if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0) { throw "msiexec failed with exit code $($proc.ExitCode)" }
          # winfsp-sys build.rs reads HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp\InstallDir
          # to find headers/libs. The MSI doesn't reliably write this key on CI runners.
          $installDir = "C:\Program Files (x86)\WinFsp"
          if (!(Test-Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp")) {
            New-Item -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Force | Out-Null
          }
          New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Name "InstallDir" -Value $installDir -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
          # Verify registry key was written correctly
          $regVal = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Name "InstallDir" -ErrorAction Stop
          if (-not $regVal.InstallDir -or $regVal.InstallDir -ne $installDir) {
            throw "WinFsp InstallDir registry mismatch: expected '$installDir', got '$($regVal.InstallDir)'"
          }
          Write-Host "WinFsp InstallDir registry: $($regVal.InstallDir)"
          if (!(Test-Path "$installDir\lib")) { throw "WinFsp lib directory not found at $installDir\lib" }
          if (!(Test-Path "$installDir\inc")) { throw "WinFsp inc directory not found at $installDir\inc" }

  deploy-vps:
    name: Deploy to Staging VPS
    needs: [build-api, build-tee, build-web]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Download web dist artifact
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: web-dist
          path: web-dist/

      - name: Generate .env.staging
        run: |
          cat > .env.staging << 'ENVEOF'
          NODE_ENV=staging
          CIPHERBOX_ENVIRONMENT=staging
          TEST_LOGIN_SECRET=${{ secrets.STAGING_TEST_LOGIN_SECRET }}
          PORT=3000
          DB_HOST=postgres
          DB_PORT=5432
          DB_USERNAME=${{ vars.STAGING_DB_USERNAME }}
          DB_PASSWORD=${{ secrets.STAGING_DB_PASSWORD }}
          DB_DATABASE=cipherbox_staging
          JWT_SECRET=${{ secrets.STAGING_JWT_SECRET }}
          CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=${{ vars.CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS }}
          IPFS_PROVIDER=local
          IPFS_LOCAL_API_URL=http://ipfs:5001
          IPFS_LOCAL_GATEWAY_URL=http://ipfs:8080
          DELEGATED_ROUTING_URL=http://someguy:8190
          REDIS_HOST=redis
          REDIS_PORT=6379
          TEE_WORKER_URL=http://tee-worker:3001
          TEE_WORKER_SECRET=${{ secrets.STAGING_TEE_WORKER_SECRET }}
          REDIS_PASSWORD=${{ secrets.STAGING_REDIS_PASSWORD }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_URL=${{ vars.GRAFANA_LOKI_URL }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME=${{ vars.GRAFANA_LOKI_USERNAME }}
          GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY=${{ secrets.GRAFANA_LOKI_API_KEY }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL=${{ vars.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_URL }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME=${{ vars.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_USERNAME }}
          GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY=${{ secrets.GRAFANA_PROMETHEUS_API_KEY }}
          SENDGRID_API_KEY=${{ secrets.SENDGRID_API_KEY }}
          SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL=${{ vars.SENDGRID_FROM_EMAIL }}
          GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=${{ vars.GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID }}
          IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY=${{ secrets.IDENTITY_JWT_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          ENVEOF
          # Append image tag and lowercase owner (can't use shell vars in quoted heredoc)
          OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
          echo "GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER=${OWNER,,}" >> .env.staging
          echo "TAG=${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}" >> .env.staging

      - name: Copy files to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@v0.1.7
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          source: '.env.staging,docker/docker-compose.staging.yml,docker/Caddyfile,docker/alloy-config.river'
          target: /opt/cipherbox
          strip_components: 0

      - name: Arrange files on VPS
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            # Move files to correct locations
            mv /opt/cipherbox/.env.staging /opt/cipherbox/docker/.env.staging 2>/dev/null || true
            cd /opt/cipherbox/docker

            # Docker Compose reads .env automatically for variable substitution
            cp .env.staging .env

            # Restrict env file permissions (contains secrets)
            chmod 600 .env .env.staging

            # Ensure certs symlink exists for Caddy
            rm -rf /opt/cipherbox/docker/certs
            ln -sf /opt/cipherbox/certs /opt/cipherbox/docker/certs

      - name: Deploy web app files to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@v0.1.7
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          source: 'web-dist/*'
          target: /opt/cipherbox/web
          strip_components: 1
          rm: true

      - name: Deploy services
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            set -euo pipefail
            cd /opt/cipherbox/docker

            # Login to GHCR
            echo "${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}" | docker login ghcr.io -u ${{ github.actor }} --password-stdin

            # Set image tag from git tag (GHCR requires lowercase owner)
            export TAG="${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}"
            OWNER="${{ github.repository_owner }}"
            export GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER="${OWNER,,}"

            # Pull new images
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml pull

            # Run database migrations before starting services
            # (api service inherits env vars from env_file in compose)
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml run --rm \
              api node dist/run-migrations.js

            # Start/restart services
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml up -d

            # Restart Caddy to pick up refreshed web files bind mount
            # (scp rm:true recreates the host dir, breaking the old mount inode)
            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml restart caddy

            # Cleanup old images
            docker image prune -f

  provision-dashboard:
    name: Provision Grafana Dashboard
    needs: [deploy-vps]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Push dashboard to Grafana Cloud
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
          DS_METRICS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID }}
          DS_LOGS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${GRAFANA_URL:?GRAFANA_URL is required}"
          : "${GRAFANA_API_KEY:?GRAFANA_API_KEY is required}"
          : "${DS_METRICS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID is required}"
          : "${DS_LOGS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID is required}"
          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"

          # The dashboard JSON uses __inputs for datasource templating.
          # Replace variable references with actual datasource UIDs.
          DASHBOARD=$(cat docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json \
            | jq --arg metrics "$DS_METRICS_UID" --arg logs "$DS_LOGS_UID" \
                 'del(.__inputs)
                  | .id = null
                  | walk(if type == "object" and .uid? and (.uid | test("\\$\\{DS_")) then
                      .uid = (if .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_METRICS}" then $metrics
                              elif .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_LOGS}" then $logs
                              else .uid end)
                    else . end)')

          # Fail if any datasource placeholder survived the rewrite
          if jq -e '.. | objects | .uid? | select(type == "string" and test("^\\$\\{DS_"))' \
            >/dev/null <<<"$DASHBOARD"; then
            echo "::error::Unresolved datasource placeholder(s) remain in dashboard JSON"
            exit 1
          fi

          # Wrap in import payload
          PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --argjson dashboard "$DASHBOARD" '{
            dashboard: $dashboard,
            overwrite: true,
            message: "Provisioned by deploy-staging workflow"
          }')

          # Push to Grafana API
          HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 \
            -o /tmp/grafana-response.json -w "%{http_code}" \
            -X POST "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/dashboards/db" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$PAYLOAD")

          if [[ ! "$HTTP_CODE" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Grafana API returned HTTP $HTTP_CODE"
            cat /tmp/grafana-response.json
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "Dashboard provisioned successfully (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)"
          jq -r '.url // "unknown"' /tmp/grafana-response.json

- name: Wait for Grafana Cloud readiness
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"
          MAX_ATTEMPTS=30
          INTERVAL=10
          for ((i=1; i<=MAX_ATTEMPTS; i++)); do
            HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 15 \
              -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
              "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/health") || HTTP_CODE=000
            if [[ "$HTTP_CODE" == "200" ]]; then
              echo "Grafana Cloud is ready (attempt $i/$MAX_ATTEMPTS)"

            echo "Grafana not ready (HTTP $HTTP_CODE), waiting ${INTERVAL}s... ($i/$MAX_ATTEMPTS)"

            HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 15 \
              -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
              "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/health") || HTTP_CODE=000

              exit 0

            echo "Grafana not ready (HTTP $HTTP_CODE), waiting ${INTERVAL}s... ($i/$MAX_ATTEMPTS)"

          echo "::error::Grafana Cloud did not become ready after $((MAX_ATTEMPTS * INTERVAL))s"

      - name: Push dashboard to Grafana Cloud
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
          DS_METRICS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID }}
          DS_LOGS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${GRAFANA_URL:?GRAFANA_URL is required}"
          : "${GRAFANA_API_KEY:?GRAFANA_API_KEY is required}"
          : "${DS_METRICS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID is required}"
          : "${DS_LOGS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID is required}"

          DASHBOARD=$(cat docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json \
            | jq --arg metrics "$DS_METRICS_UID" --arg logs "$DS_LOGS_UID" \

                      .uid = (if .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_METRICS}" then $metrics
                              elif .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_LOGS}" then $logs
                              else .uid end)
                    else . end)')

          # Fail if any datasource placeholder survived the rewrite
          if jq -e '.. | objects | .uid? | select(type == "string" and test("^\\$\\{DS_"))' \
            >/dev/null <<<"$DASHBOARD"; then
            echo "::error::Unresolved datasource placeholder(s) remain in dashboard JSON"
            exit 1
          fi

          # Wrap in import payload
          PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --argjson dashboard "$DASHBOARD" '{
            dashboard: $dashboard,
            overwrite: true,
            message: "Provisioned by deploy-staging workflow"
          }')

          # Push to Grafana API
          HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 \
            -o /tmp/grafana-response.json -w "%{http_code}" \
            -X POST "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/dashboards/db" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$PAYLOAD")

            cat /tmp/grafana-response.json
            exit 1
          fi

name: Deploy Staging

on:

env:

  DEPLOY_TAG: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

jobs:
  build-api:
    name: Build & Push API Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Set lowercase image name
        run: echo "API_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-api" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:
          context: .
          file: apps/api/Dockerfile
          push: true
          tags: |
            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}
            ${{ env.API_IMAGE }}:latest

  build-tee:
    name: Build & Push TEE Worker Image
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - name: Set lowercase image name
        run: echo "TEE_IMAGE=ghcr.io/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY_OWNER,,}/cipherbox-tee-worker" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - uses: docker/login-action@v3
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5

            ${{ env.TEE_IMAGE }}:${{ env.DEPLOY_TAG }}

  build-web:
    name: Build Web App
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: staging
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

          ref: ${{ inputs.staging_tag || github.ref_name }}

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v4
        with:
          version: 10

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies

      - name: Build shared packages
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/core build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/api-client build
          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk-core build

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install WinFsp
        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          # Use Join-Path to produce proper Windows backslash paths —
          # msiexec.exe treats '/' as a flag prefix, so forward slashes in
          # the file path cause "package could not be opened" errors.
          $resourceDir = Join-Path "${{ github.workspace }}" "apps\desktop\src-tauri\resources"
          $out = Join-Path $resourceDir "winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $resourceDir
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
          if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch: expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash" }
          $proc = Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","`"$out`"","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow -PassThru
          if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0) { throw "msiexec failed with exit code $($proc.ExitCode)" }
          # winfsp-sys build.rs reads HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp\InstallDir

          $installDir = "C:\Program Files (x86)\WinFsp"
          if (!(Test-Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp")) {
            New-Item -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Force | Out-Null
          }
          New-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Name "InstallDir" -Value $installDir -PropertyType String -Force | Out-Null
          # Verify registry key was written correctly
          $regVal = Get-ItemProperty -Path "HKLM:\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp" -Name "InstallDir" -ErrorAction Stop
          if (-not $regVal.InstallDir -or $regVal.InstallDir -ne $installDir) {
            throw "WinFsp InstallDir registry mismatch: expected '$installDir', got '$($regVal.InstallDir)'"
          }
          Write-Host "WinFsp InstallDir registry: $($regVal.InstallDir)"
          if (!(Test-Path "$installDir\lib")) { throw "WinFsp lib directory not found at $installDir\lib" }
          if (!(Test-Path "$installDir\inc")) { throw "WinFsp inc directory not found at $installDir\inc" }

      - name: Install Rust toolchain

      - uses: actions/cache@v4

          cache: 'pnpm'

      - name: Install dependencies

      - name: Build shared packages

          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/crypto build

          pnpm --filter @cipherbox/sdk build

      - uses: tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID: ${{ vars.VITE_WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID }}

content.text:
PR created: https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/320

The fix adds a "Wait for Grafana Cloud readiness" step that polls `/api/health` every 10 seconds for up to 5 minutes before attempting the dashboard push. This handles the free-tier instance wake-up delay that was causing the consistent 503s.

# Resolve PR Review Comments

Resolve all open review comments on the current PR from any automated reviewer (CodeRabbit, GitHub Copilot, etc.) or human reviewers.

## Workflow

### 1. Identify the PR

```bash
PR_NUMBER=$(gh pr view --json number --jq '.number')
```

If no PR exists for the current branch, stop and inform the user.

### 2. Fetch all unresolved review threads

Use the GraphQL `reviewThreads` query to get threads with `isResolved` status:

```bash
REPO_OWNER=$(gh repo view --json owner --jq '.owner.login')
REPO_NAME=$(gh repo view --json name --jq '.name')

gh api graphql -f query="
{
  repository(owner: \"$REPO_OWNER\", name: \"$REPO_NAME\") {
    pullRequest(number: $PR_NUMBER) {
      reviewThreads(first: 100) {
        nodes {
          id
          isResolved
          comments(first: 10) {
            nodes {
              id
              author { login }
              body
              path
              line
              createdAt
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}"
```

Filter to only unresolved threads. If none, report "No unresolved review threads" and stop.

### 3. Triage each comment

For each unresolved thread, read the comment and the referenced code. Categorize as:

- **Valid fix needed** — the comment identifies a real bug, security issue, or meaningful improvement
- **Already addressed** — the issue was fixed in a later commit on this branch
- **Not applicable** — the suggestion doesn't apply (explain why)

### 4. Implement fixes

For all "valid fix needed" comments:

1. Read the referenced file and understand the context
2. Implement the fix
3. Track which thread the fix addresses

Do NOT:

- Make unrelated changes or refactors
- Add features beyond what the comment requests
- Increase timeouts or add retries as a first approach — fix root causes

### 5. Run tests locally

After ALL fixes are implemented:

```bash
# Type check
pnpm typecheck

# Run relevant unit tests
pnpm test

# If E2E-relevant changes were made, run E2E tests too
cd tests/web-e2e && pnpm exec playwright test
```

Do NOT proceed to commit until tests pass. If tests fail, fix the failures first.

### 6. Commit and push

```bash
git add <specific-files>
git commit -m "fix: address PR review comments"
git push
```

### 7. Reply to and resolve each thread

For each thread, reply explaining what was done, then resolve:

- **Fixed comments**: Reply with what was changed and where, then resolve
- **Already addressed**: Reply explaining which commit addressed it, then resolve
- **Not applicable**: Reply with clear reasoning for not making changes, then resolve

Reply via REST (use `--field` not `-f` for `in_reply_to` — must be integer):

```bash
gh api repos/$REPO_OWNER/$REPO_NAME/pulls/$PR_NUMBER/comments \
  --field in_reply_to=COMMENT_ID \
  --raw-field body='...'
```

Resolve via GraphQL (can batch multiple):

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
mutation {
  resolveReviewThread(input: {threadId: "THREAD_ID"}) {
    thread { isResolved }
  }
}'
```

### 8. Report summary

Print a summary table:

- Thread count resolved
- Fixes made (with file:line references)
- Comments marked as already addressed or not applicable
I'll start by identifying the PR and fetching unresolved review threads.

Three unresolved threads. Let me triage them:

1. **Copilot #1** (line 514): Add env var validation — valid, easy fix
2. **Copilot #2** (line 525): Fail fast on 401/403/404 — valid, good suggestion
3. **CodeRabbit** (line 531): Deadline-based timeout — over-engineered for this use case. 30 attempts x (15s max curl + 10s sleep) = 12.5 min theoretical max, but in practice each curl returns in <1s. The attempt-based approach is clear enough and 5 min is a soft target, not a hard SLA. I'll skip the deadline rewrite but the other two fixes are worth making.

- name: Wait for Grafana Cloud readiness
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"
          MAX_ATTEMPTS=30
          INTERVAL=10
          for ((i=1; i<=MAX_ATTEMPTS; i++)); do
            HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 15 \
              -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
              "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/health") || HTTP_CODE=000
            if [[ "$HTTP_CODE" == "200" ]]; then
              echo "Grafana Cloud is ready (attempt $i/$MAX_ATTEMPTS)"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "Grafana not ready (HTTP $HTTP_CODE), waiting ${INTERVAL}s... ($i/$MAX_ATTEMPTS)"
            sleep "$INTERVAL"
          done
          echo "::error::Grafana Cloud did not become ready after $((MAX_ATTEMPTS * INTERVAL))s"
          exit 1

      - name: Push dashboard to Grafana Cloud
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
          DS_METRICS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID }}
          DS_LOGS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID }}

name: Deploy Staging

env:

      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v5
        with:

        shell: powershell
        run: |
          $url = "https://github.com/winfsp/winfsp/releases/download/v2.1/winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          # Use Join-Path to produce proper Windows backslash paths —
          # msiexec.exe treats '/' as a flag prefix, so forward slashes in
          # the file path cause "package could not be opened" errors.
          $resourceDir = Join-Path "${{ github.workspace }}" "apps\desktop\src-tauri\resources"
          $out = Join-Path $resourceDir "winfsp-2.1.25156.msi"
          $expectedHash = "073A70E00F77423E34BED98B86E600DEF93393BA5822204FAC57A29324DB9F7A"
          New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $resourceDir
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $url -OutFile $out
          $actualHash = (Get-FileHash $out -Algorithm SHA256).Hash
          if ($actualHash -ne $expectedHash) { throw "WinFsp MSI hash mismatch: expected $expectedHash, got $actualHash" }
          $proc = Start-Process msiexec.exe -ArgumentList "/i","`"$out`"","/qn","INSTALLLEVEL=1000" -Wait -NoNewWindow -PassThru
          if ($proc.ExitCode -ne 0) { throw "msiexec failed with exit code $($proc.ExitCode)" }
          # winfsp-sys build.rs reads HKLM\SOFTWARE\WOW6432Node\WinFsp\InstallDir

          $installDir = "C:\Program Files (x86)\WinFsp"

          # Verify registry key was written correctly

            throw "WinFsp InstallDir registry mismatch: expected '$installDir', got '$($regVal.InstallDir)'"

          Write-Host "WinFsp InstallDir registry: $($regVal.InstallDir)"
          if (!(Test-Path "$installDir\lib")) { throw "WinFsp lib directory not found at $installDir\lib" }
          if (!(Test-Path "$installDir\inc")) { throw "WinFsp inc directory not found at $installDir\inc" }

    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:

        run: |

          ENVEOF

      - name: Copy files to VPS
        uses: appleboy/scp-action@v0.1.7
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}
          username: ${{ vars.STAGING_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.STAGING_SSH_KEY }}
          source: '.env.staging,docker/docker-compose.staging.yml,docker/Caddyfile,docker/alloy-config.river'
          target: /opt/cipherbox
          strip_components: 0

      - name: Arrange files on VPS
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.2.0
        with:
          host: ${{ vars.STAGING_HOST }}

            docker compose -f docker-compose.staging.yml run --rm \
              api node dist/run-migrations.js

            # (scp rm:true recreates the host dir, breaking the old mount inode)

    name: Provision Grafana Dashboard
    needs: [deploy-vps]

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

        env:

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"
          MAX_ATTEMPTS=30
          INTERVAL=10
          for ((i=1; i<=MAX_ATTEMPTS; i++)); do
            HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 15 \
              -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" \
              -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
              "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/health") || HTTP_CODE=000
            if [[ "$HTTP_CODE" == "200" ]]; then
              echo "Grafana Cloud is ready (attempt $i/$MAX_ATTEMPTS)"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "Grafana not ready (HTTP $HTTP_CODE), waiting ${INTERVAL}s... ($i/$MAX_ATTEMPTS)"
            sleep "$INTERVAL"
          done
          echo "::error::Grafana Cloud did not become ready after $((MAX_ATTEMPTS * INTERVAL))s"
          exit 1

      - name: Push dashboard to Grafana Cloud
        env:
          GRAFANA_URL: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_URL }}
          GRAFANA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GRAFANA_API_KEY }}
          DS_METRICS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID }}
          DS_LOGS_UID: ${{ vars.GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          : "${GRAFANA_URL:?GRAFANA_URL is required}"
          : "${GRAFANA_API_KEY:?GRAFANA_API_KEY is required}"
          : "${DS_METRICS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_METRICS_UID is required}"
          : "${DS_LOGS_UID:?GRAFANA_DS_LOGS_UID is required}"
          GRAFANA_URL="${GRAFANA_URL%/}"

          # The dashboard JSON uses __inputs for datasource templating.
          # Replace variable references with actual datasource UIDs.
          DASHBOARD=$(cat docker/grafana/dashboards/cipherbox-staging.json \
            | jq --arg metrics "$DS_METRICS_UID" --arg logs "$DS_LOGS_UID" \
                 'del(.__inputs)
                  | .id = null
                  | walk(if type == "object" and .uid? and (.uid | test("\\$\\{DS_")) then
                      .uid = (if .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_METRICS}" then $metrics
                              elif .uid == "${DS_GRAFANA_CLOUD_LOGS}" then $logs
                              else .uid end)
                    else . end)')

          # Fail if any datasource placeholder survived the rewrite
          if jq -e '.. | objects | .uid? | select(type == "string" and test("^\\$\\{DS_"))' \
            >/dev/null <<<"$DASHBOARD"; then
            echo "::error::Unresolved datasource placeholder(s) remain in dashboard JSON"
            exit 1
          fi

          # Wrap in import payload
          PAYLOAD=$(jq -n --argjson dashboard "$DASHBOARD" '{
            dashboard: $dashboard,
            overwrite: true,
            message: "Provisioned by deploy-staging workflow"
          }')

          # Push to Grafana API
          HTTP_CODE=$(curl -sS --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 \
            -o /tmp/grafana-response.json -w "%{http_code}" \
            -X POST "${GRAFANA_URL}/api/dashboards/db" \
            -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GRAFANA_API_KEY}" \
            -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
            -d "$PAYLOAD")

          if [[ ! "$HTTP_CODE" =~ ^2[0-9][0-9]$ ]]; then
            echo "::error::Grafana API returned HTTP $HTTP_CODE"
            cat /tmp/grafana-response.json
            exit 1
          fi

          echo "Dashboard provisioned successfully (HTTP $HTTP_CODE)"
          jq -r '.url // "unknown"' /tmp/grafana-response.json
